title: /grade commit step skips unchanged verdict files
item: Step 4 of commands/grade.md commits only verdict files that are new or changed, so an unusable verdict that grade.py re-lists does not make git commit fail
motivation: grade.py re-lists a judge task whose verdict file exists but is unusable (error field, empty or all-null items). Step 4 takes every listed task's existing verdict file, so if the only one is already committed and unchanged, git commit exits 1 with nothing to commit. Found by the task 20 reviewer.
notes: The test builds <paths> with its own code, not from the pattern in grade.md; the fix could close that gap too.
done_means: When every listed verdict file is already committed and unchanged, /grade step 4 makes no commit and does not fail. A test in a temporary git repo covers that case.
draft_note: Drafted by the manager on 2026-11-15 from the task 20 review. Priority left for the owner.

needs_you.question: Verification still fails after the one retry. Branch task/036 (commits 7416407, 3ca9709) meets done_means: committed, unchanged verdicts give no commit, an empty <found> runs no git command, and 6 tests pass. The second review failed it on: (1) the test never checks grade.md's 'If <paths> is empty ... make no commit' sentence, so deleting it keeps every test green; (2) `git status --porcelain -z` misses untracked verdicts under status.showUntrackedFiles=no and may print a folder on git < 2.27; add --untracked-files=all; (3) an agent reading -z output in a tool result may not see the NUL separators; (4) the parse rule ignores staged renames. Should the next run retry with these four fixes?
needs_you.recommendation: Yes: drop -z and use `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- <found>` (verdict paths are <label>/judge/<metric>.verdict.json, plain characters), add an ordering test for the empty-<paths> sentence, and set the task back to Ready for one more build on task/036.
needs_you.if_vetoed: If you accept the branch as it is, the next run merges task/036 unchanged and the four points become one Proposed task. If you prefer keeping -z, the retry pipes it through tr '\0' '\n' instead.

decided_for_you.chosen: Filter found verdict files with git status before add/commit
Use -z and state how to read it (retry)
decided_for_you.rejected: Explain unquoting of plain porcelain output
decided_for_you.would_change: The second review: NUL output is hard for an agent to read; recommendation above drops -z

decided_for_you.chosen: Extra tests for a partly changed set, no verdict found, and unusual path characters
decided_for_you.would_change: You want only the done_means test
